principle: Once a latent or generated thing becomes a persistent concrete entity, its identity is never rerolled or silently replaced. It may evolve only through authoritative state/history.

forbidden_examples: change_species_without explicit world event and supported rules
replace_ship identity after repair or refit
discard history when entity leaves simulation LOD

deterministic_rules: Identity-affecting generation uses stable derived seeds tied to entity_id and subsystem/version.
Adding unrelated generator subsystems must not change an existing entity identity.
Loading, unloading, LOD changes, travel, save/load and offline catch-up must not reroll identity.
Rules upgrades require explicit migration; they cannot silently regenerate existing identities.
history_rules: Persistent change is represented as authoritative state mutation and/or historical event.
Current presentation is resolved from persistent identity plus accumulated changes plus temporary state.
If an entity is encountered years later, the system resolves the same entity at the later date.
Death, destruction or retirement ends active participation but does not erase identity or history.
core_rpg_boundary: Generic persistent identity, history and migration semantics belong in CoreRPG; Star Trek owns Trek-specific identity anchors, species/canon constraints and presentation rules.
